terms.gloss: a partner, an associate; in business, a co-partner
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Com. 16: socium fallere quī sē in negōtiō conjūnxit
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “fellow, sharer, partner, comrade, companion, associate (very freq. and class.)”; in the language of trade, a partner in business. Feminine socia.

terms.gloss: a colleague: properly a partner in office
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.144: cum habēret collēgam in praetūrā Sophoclem
terms.comment: Classically one who holds the same office; by extension, an associate in a school or a craft (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Fam. 13.78.1: nōn sōlum hospes meus est, sed etiam … valdē familiāris

phrases.latin: Aequē enim perfidiōsum et nefārium est fidem frangere quae continet vītam, et pupillum fraudāre quī in tūtēlam pervēnit, et socium fallere quī sē in negōtiō conjūnxit.
phrases.english: For it is equally treacherous and wicked to break the trust that holds life together, to cheat a ward who has come into one’s care, and to deceive a partner who has joined one in business.

phrases.latin: Bene Periclēs, cum habēret collēgam in praetūrā Sophoclem poētam …
phrases.english: Pericles did well, when he had the poet Sophocles as his colleague in command …
